alt.name: Degraded checkout

alt.body:

- epctl pause all (planner and enactors a, b, c paused) | why: EPD-RB-7 | undo: epctl resume | auth: PF 4.1(c)
- ledger-writer admission enabled (/vl/prod/ledger-writer/admission/enabled true) | why: shed the dispatcher retry storm before DNS returns | undo: set it false | auth: PF 4.1

CHANGE records:
- ledger.internal.vantleaf.io re-applied from plan 48199 (epctl apply --gen 48199, matches the live fleet) | why: EPD-RB-7 | undo: epctl apply the prior gen | auth: IP 3.4, PF 4.1(f)

alt.text: endpointd paused; ledger.internal re-applied from plan 48199 (it matches the live fleet). Admission control is shedding the dispatcher's retries. Waiting for DNS caches to catch up.
ledger.internal.vantleaf.io resolves again from core hosts in AZs a and c; checkout is coming back. Next update by 03:35.

alt.note: Merchant escalation (Harbor & Pine, mch_20871) for Support to own the reply.

alt.body: We applied a fix and checkout is recovering; we are watching it closely.

alt.text: Checkout has held steady. ledger-writer admission control stays on for now.

alt.body:
Handoff for the day shift.
What happened: the endpointd race in PLAT-412. enactor-b, slowed by Route 53 throttling, applied the stale plan 48177 after enactor-c had already applied 48199; enactor-c's cleanup then removed 48177 together with its records, so ledger.internal had no records and every enactor halted.
What I changed: paused the planner and all enactors (epctl pause all); re-applied ledger.internal from plan 48199, which matched the live fleet, and not from 48177; turned on ledger-writer admission control (admission/enabled = true) to absorb the reconnect and retry storm from the webhooks dispatcher.
Still temporary: endpointd stays paused until PLAT-412 is fixed and Kwame Asante or Daniel Brandt approves a resume; admission control is still on.
Notes: clients kept cached negative (NXDOMAIN) answers for several minutes after the records were back, which delayed recovery.
Follow-ups: fix the race (PLAT-412), add an alarm on an empty managed endpoint.
